purpose: Optional source-preserving image styling and interchangeable game asset variants; templates only, no generated assets.

prompts.intent: Decide whether source artwork can be used unchanged.
reference_requirements: The actual supplied image and intended use.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} for use as {{INTENDED_ROLE}} in {{DEVICE_CONTEXT}}. Describe only what is actually visible: medium, subjects, markings, focal anchors, quiet areas and crop-sensitive details. Read the actual file dimensions when available; separate measured facts from suggested runtime sizes. Start with keep-source and a separate gameplay overlay. Explain whether a border/underlay or different fit would provide sufficient legibility without repainting. Offer requested styling only as optional named derivatives, and do not generate or upload anything during this review. A supplied photograph can remain a photograph. If X or ^ is an object placeholder, determine its role from the supplied level brief rather than treating it as mandatory final artwork. Report uncertainty in subject identity or allegiance instead of guessing. Deliver a short source record, preservation plan and concrete visual concerns; no claim of collision or device validation follows from one picture. For current FPV FRONT inputs, check the project direction of no Z markings anywhere and keep Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral identity explicit in the authoring record; preserve the original even when a separate correction is needed.
prompts.example_request: Use this photograph in the game and tell me what needs adapting.

prompts.intent: Make a requested local correction without redesigning the source.
reference_requirements: The source image and a specific correction request.
prompts.prompt: Edit {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} only to make this requested correction: {{REQUESTED_CORRECTION}}. Preserve {{PRESERVE_DETAILS}}, the composition, subject identities, visual medium, lighting direction and focal relationships unless the requested correction explicitly changes one of them. Avoid automatically introducing pixel texture, neon outlines, new text or a cinematic camera. Treat a background cleanup as a separate derived image; retain the unedited source. For current FPV FRONT material, remove unintended Z markings and introduce none elsewhere; identify Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral objects from the supplied brief, never from an improvised visual assumption. Leave runtime mask boundaries and object colliders outside this edit. After generation inspect the changed region and distant details for unintended drift, then record the actual output dimensions and any failed preservation requirement. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. Use the built-in image tool for requested image editing; do not upload to public hosting or fall back to a third-party API/CLI automatically. Record the effective prompt, parent/source, tool route, actual output dimensions and manual review. Artwork never changes gameplay geometry, colliders or behavior. A concept is not a production-ready sprite. For current FPV FRONT inputs, check the project direction of no Z markings anywhere and keep Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral identity explicit in the authoring record; preserve the original even when a separate correction is needed.
prompts.example_request: Remove the unwanted marking but keep the scene and watercolor style intact.

prompts.intent: Produce an explicitly requested pixel-art interpretation.
reference_requirements: The original image and the requested pixel-art direction.
prompts.prompt: Create a separate pixel-art interpretation of {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} following {{PIXEL_DIRECTION}}. This conversion is requested; it must not replace the original or become a compulsory import step. Preserve {{FOCAL_DETAILS}}, composition, perspective, subject identities and the overall light/dark map. Use deliberate pixel clusters and readable material shapes rather than applying coarse noise or a blur-to-mosaic filter. Keep the underlying picture expressive while reserving calm regions for the player and active trail; do not bake the game HUD or mask into the artwork. Show large silhouette relationships clearly at the intended small scale. If the source contains text, leave reliable localization to separate assets unless exact text preservation is required and visibly verified. Do not claim a generated image has a precise native pixel grid until measured and inspected. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. Use the built-in image tool for requested image editing; do not upload to public hosting or fall back to a third-party API/CLI automatically. Record the effective prompt, parent/source, tool route, actual output dimensions and manual review. Artwork never changes gameplay geometry, colliders or behavior. A concept is not a production-ready sprite. For current FPV FRONT inputs, check the project direction of no Z markings anywhere and keep Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral identity explicit in the authoring record; preserve the original even when a separate correction is needed.
prompts.example_request: Make an optional 16-bit chapter variant of this scene while keeping the original.

prompts.intent: Explore a painted variant while preserving the same scene.
reference_requirements: The source image and requested paint medium.
prompts.prompt: Create an optional {{PAINT_MEDIUM}} derivative of {{SOURCE_IMAGE}}, preserving {{PRESERVED_SUBJECTS}}, their arrangement, the horizon and the scene’s focal hierarchy. The result should read as the requested medium through edge handling, pigment or brush character and material-specific light; do not add a generic pixel grid or forced neon. Maintain enough subdued areas for a separate arcade overlay without erasing meaningful scene detail. Keep all game controls, collision regions, active enemy markers and capture boundaries out of the background image. If the composition needs a different device crop, propose that crop as a separate derivative rather than destructively cutting the source. In FPV FRONT imagery preserve the requested invading military presence and apply the current no-Z direction to every object. Compare the output against the source for missing subjects and changed identities. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. prompts.intent: Keep photography intact and design the arcade overlay separately.
reference_requirements: The photograph and known board/layout context.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} and prepare a keep-source plan for {{BOARD_CONTEXT}} with the separate overlay palette {{OVERLAY_PALETTE}}. Retain the photograph’s medium, faces or objects, perspective, tones and original file. Describe fit versus crop options with focal tradeoffs, and recommend a quiet optional underlay only where gameplay markers need it. Specify player, trail, claimed-boundary and live-threat presentation independently from the photograph; decorative vehicles or objects do not become enemies. The plan may suggest a reversible derived color treatment, but do not create it unless requested. Separate the original image dimensions from the proposed display size and logical board cells. If rendering fixtures exist, inspect small initial reveal, partial reveal and gallery states; otherwise label these reviews pending. Full-gallery visibility does not alter captured percentage. Deliver a proposed overlay/crop record, not a claim that a photographed background requires AI restyling. For current FPV FRONT inputs, check the project direction of no Z markings anywhere and keep Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral identity explicit in the authoring record; preserve the original even when a separate correction is needed.
prompts.example_request: Use the supplied photo as it is, with readable pixel characters on top.

prompts.intent: Correct faction identity and remove conflicting markings.
reference_requirements: Source image, per-entity allegiance brief and the exact requested correction.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} against the supplied entity map {{ENTITY_ALLEGIANCE_MAP}} and make only {{REQUESTED_IDENTITY_FIX}}. The map must distinguish Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral entities; leave ambiguous entities unconfirmed rather than assigning identity from a vehicle silhouette. Apply the current FPV FRONT direction: no Z markings anywhere, including background vehicles, wings, props, fabric, tiny decals or decorative glyphs. Ukrainian drones and equipment must never acquire hostile insignia. Preserve the source’s declared medium, composition, subject count, relative sizes and lighting unless the requested fix says otherwise. Use restrained, clearly intentional Ukrainian identification when requested by the entity map; do not invent official unit insignia. Retain hostile military presence where the source brief requires it, but distinguish it through the approved entity treatment rather than conflicting symbols. Review every visible asset after editing; metadata must reflect the intended identity, not excuse an incorrect picture. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. Use the built-in image tool for requested image editing; do not upload to public hosting or fall back to a third-party API/CLI automatically. Record the effective prompt, parent/source, tool route, actual output dimensions and manual review. Artwork never changes gameplay geometry, colliders or behavior. A concept is not a production-ready sprite.
prompts.example_request: Fix the Ukrainian drone identity and remove every Z marking from this concept.

Change only the requested chapter aesthetic—such as dawn palette, winter atmosphere or night illumination—while preserving focal subjects, camera, composition and the objects needed for visual discovery. Avoid photoreal operational overlays or real targeting data; this is an arcade-art background. Keep collision objects, active drone markers and capture contours on a separate layer defined by game data. Match the source medium unless a medium change is explicitly included in the chapter request. Inspect the derived result against the source and distinguish it from a tested game screenshot. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. prompts.example_request: Create Daybreak and Winter Signal variants of the same FPV scene.

Decorative cultural detail belongs in the picture or a restrained frame, while the live trail and enemy symbols remain separate. Keep cultural subjects out of enemy roles. Verify unfamiliar factual motifs from suitable references before claiming authenticity, and record which elements are original interpretation. Provide one coherent derivative per requested medium, not several unrelated scenes. If the source is photographic and the request is only for a retro frame, preserve the source pixels and return a separate frame/overlay plan. Do not bake controls or level geometry into the background. Compare the derivative at small display size and preserve calm space for separate gameplay markers. reference_requirements: Source background, business scene brief and any available approved character reference.
prompts.prompt: Create a separate NAVI NETWORK variant of {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} following {{BUSINESS_SCENE_DIRECTION}}. Preserve the source’s scene structure, subjects and intended workflow meaning. Live obstacles represent process friction, not customers, suppliers or employees. Savings tokens and scores are fictional game values, and generated artwork must not contain fabricated customer results or invoice text. X, ^, a square or another simple glyph may stand for a game object; use its declared semantic role instead of preserving the glyph literally or assuming it identifies a faction. Keep each object’s logical anchor, facing convention, draw order, collider size, movement domain and fill-blocking behavior unchanged. Design recognizable silhouettes within the existing art bounds; if a larger drawing needs overhang, record that as visual padding rather than enlarging the collider. Keep scenery objects and live entities distinguishable at small scale. For FPV assets record allegiance explicitly and apply no Z markings anywhere. Deliver skins as separate derivatives, preserving the reference and a comparison fixture; do not claim transparent export or atlas readiness without file inspection. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. If this is a Coupa placeholder, distinguish concept identity from an authenticated Navi likeness. Preserve the source and save each alternative separately. Review tiny-size readability, direction consistency and cut-trail attachment; note alpha, frame alignment and animation as untested unless actually inspected. prompts.intent: Vary terrain materials while preserving their exact meanings.
reference_requirements: Terrain reference and explicit role/footprint map.
prompts.prompt: Create a separate terrain-visual sheet from {{SOURCE_IMAGE}} using {{TERRAIN_ROLE_MAP}} and {{FAMILY_STYLE}}. Preserve every tile’s logical footprint and declared behavior; changing a tile’s appearance never changes collisions or coverage rules. Keep solid walls, player-only slowing fields and player-lethal fields visually distinct. Walls block player and enemy movement where the rules specify; slow and lethal fields must not acquire an implied effect on enemies. Use different shapes/material patterns rather than relying only on red versus blue. In a material or ethnic chapter, adapt the same meanings through texture and silhouette rather than forcing neon. X or ^ may indicate an object placeholder in the role map, not decoration to bake into all tiles. Where the runtime lacks one of these behaviors, label the role proposed/extension-needed in the handoff and omit unsupported bindings from valid packs. Inspect actual seams, alpha and margins before claiming tile readiness. Inspect the supplied reference before use, preserve the original, and save any requested visual changes as separate derivatives linked to their parent asset. Use the built-in image tool for requested image editing; do not upload to public hosting or fall back to a third-party API/CLI automatically. prompts.example_request: Make ceramic and circuit-board skins for the same wall, slow and lethal tiles.

prompts.intent: Distinguish attractive object art from usable sprite exports.
reference_requirements: Actual image files and the declared role/geometry/export record.
prompts.prompt: Review {{ASSET_FILES}} against {{ROLE_GEOMETRY_RECORD}}. Inspect actual image files and measure dimensions; do not trust a generator’s declared size or a diagram label. Separate concept illustrations from exported sprite frames. Check real alpha, edge halos, equal cell sizes, padding, pivots, facing, frame order, declared timing and seams where relevant. A checkerboard painted into an image is not transparency. Compare the visual anchor with the unchanged logical collider and identify excessive silhouette overhang without editing collision data. For animated sprites, play or render the available frames before claiming animation readiness; otherwise say not-tested. Check intended texture filtering and whether pixel sprites are mixed with smooth artwork in a texture that cannot support separate filtering. For current FPV assets inspect identity and no-Z compliance. Return exact file-level findings, measured facts and the smallest corrections. Do not generate replacement art or upload assets as part of this review unless requested.
prompts.example_request: Tell me which variants are usable sprites and which are still concept art.

prompts.intent: Compare source and variants in actual reveal contexts.
reference_requirements: Actual composited fixtures plus the source/variant provenance records.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{COMPOSITE_FIXTURES}} with {{VARIANT_RECORDS}} and compare the unchanged source against the proposed style variants. Use actual supplied board fixtures for initial reveal, intermediate coverage and complete gallery display where available; report missing states as untested. Locate player, active trail, claimed boundary, field mover, contour patrol, revealed-ground mover, erosion warning and objectives only when those roles are present. Check whether a photograph or painted vehicle is confused with a live enemy, and whether wall/slow/lethal symbols remain distinct. Review small-screen readability and crop loss at the fixture’s actual display size; do not certify usability from an attractive generated device mockup. Do not rank pixel art above photography by default: recommend the version that preserves the requested identity and makes the action readable. Full artwork on victory must keep the actual captured percentage separate. Propose a small overlay or derived correction before replacing the entire image. For current FPV FRONT inputs, check the project direction of no Z markings anywhere and keep Ukrainian, hostile-military and neutral identity explicit in the authoring record; preserve the original even when a separate correction is needed.
prompts.example_request: Compare the original photo, watercolor and pixel versions under the same game overlay.

prompts.intent: Create a traceable asset-family record without inventing pack support.
reference_requirements: Existing source record, actual derivative outputs and the current content contract.
prompts.prompt: Using {{SOURCE_RECORD}}, {{VARIANT_OUTPUTS}} and {{CONTENT_CONTRACT}}, prepare an asset-variant handoff. Retain the source as the parent and assign each derivative its own stable ID; record family/chapter, semantic role, requested changes, preserved details, template ID, substitutions, full effective prompt, tool route, supplied references, actual output path/format/dimensions, intended sampling and manual review. Keep requested dimensions separate from measurements. Record source provenance honestly and preserve unknowns. For FPV assets annotate Ukrainian, hostile-military, neutral or unconfirmed allegiance per relevant entity, and report the no-Z visual check. Preserve logical anchors, colliders, movement domains and behavior references when swapping skins. Distinguish planned, generated concept, reviewed concept and production-ready-with-evidence; map to the contract’s actual accepted fields/status values only when registering a pack. Keep unsupported fields in the authoring handoff rather than fabricating schema support. Link unresolved alpha, sprite, cropping and device checks. Report validation separately from visual review and never claim a generation step that did not run.
prompts.example_request: Register these variants while keeping the original and all gameplay rules intact.
